application.name: Breakable Flask

purpose.summary: A deliberately vulnerable web application used as a compact test bed for learning and checking exploitation of common web application vulnerability classes.
evidence: README.md:1 names the project Breakable Flask.
README.md:4 describes it as a simple vulnerable Flask application.
README.md:6-8 state that it is used to test and learn exploitation of common web application vulnerabilities and was intended as a single-file vulnerable app.

primaryFunctionality: Index page listing vulnerable feature routes
Cookie set/read workflow using pickle serialization
DNS lookup workflow using an operating-system command
Personalized greeting rendered through a Jinja template string
Products/services listing backed by SQL tables
JWT login, token verification, and JWKS publication workflow

inferredRuntimeRelationships.relationship: The global cursor created at startup is shared by /listservices requests.
inferredRuntimeRelationships.basis: The cursor variable is assigned in main.py:647 and referenced by listservices at main.py:484. Python name resolution makes this a module-global variable when the script has executed the startup block.
inferredRuntimeRelationships.confidence: inferred from Python runtime semantics and direct references

inferredRuntimeRelationships.relationship: Routes depending on cursor/query_build require the script startup block to have run.
inferredRuntimeRelationships.basis: query_build and cursor are assigned under if __name__ == '__main__' at main.py:594 and main.py:647, while /listservices references them at main.py:484.

assumptionsAndUnknowns.item: Runtime behavior under import by an external WSGI server
assumptionsAndUnknowns.reason: The database bootstrap and cursor/query_build definitions are inside if __name__ == '__main__'. If imported without executing the script block, routes exist but /listservices would not have the observed startup-created cursor.
requirements files specify lower bounds, not a lockfile.
